Fix an integer $d\ge1$ and a smooth $d$-manifold $M$, possibly with boundary. Fix the metric and signature, orientation and any time orientation, the geometric background bundles or lifts required by the model, and the boundary conditions. A **selected model** $\mathcal T$ on $M$ consists of a specified configuration space $\mathcal C_{\mathcal T}(M)$ of fields, including each field bundle, regularity class, and admissible boundary behavior; a collection of local observables with their types and supports; a set $\mathcal B_{\mathcal T}$ of admissible combined background and boundary data; and a set $\mathcal A_{\mathcal T}$ of admissible complete insertion inputs. An element of $\mathcal A_{\mathcal T}$ records data $b\in\mathcal B_{\mathcal T}$ and a finite ordered list whose entries are local observable insertions or other model-declared insertion data, together with the model's admissibility conditions on supports and labels. The model supplies a value space $\mathcal V_{\mathcal T}$ with a specified topology and a correlator functional $C_{\mathcal T}:\mathcal A_{\mathcal T}\to\mathcal V_{\mathcal T}$ with an explicit normalization convention, which may be normalized or unnormalized; the notation $C_{\mathcal T}(b;D;X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ denotes its value on the complete input with combined background and boundary data $b$, defect data $D$, and other insertion data $X_i$. The model also fixes its unit system, action and charge normalizations, and any regulator, measure, or renormalization prescription used to define $C_{\mathcal T}$. These are model inputs: this definition does not construct them or assume a general interacting continuum theory exists.

A **defect insertion** in $\mathcal T$ is data $(j,\lambda)$ where $j:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M^\circ$ is a smooth embedding of a manifold $\Sigma$ without boundary whose image is closed in the interior $M^\circ=M\setminus\partial M$, and $\lambda$ is the complete model-specified field, operator, or boundary-condition data supported on $j(\Sigma)$, including any orientation, coorientation, framing, or label-transport rule the model requires. Its codimension is $d-\dim\Sigma$. It is an allowed entry of $\mathcal A_{\mathcal T}$ only when the model defines $C_{\mathcal T}(b;D_{j,\lambda};O_1,\ldots,O_n)$ for each stated admissible combined background and boundary datum $b$ and list of other insertions.

A **defect network** is data $D=(K,\{S_s,j_s,\lambda_s\}_{s\in S},\{J_t\}_{t\in J})$ in which $K\subset M^\circ$ is closed, $S$ is finite, $K=\bigsqcup_{s\in S}S_s$ is a smooth stratification, and each $j_s:\Sigma_s\to S_s$ is a diffeomorphism from a smooth manifold without boundary onto its locally closed embedded stratum. The closure of each stratum is a union of strata, with the frontier condition that if $S_t$ meets the closure of $S_s$ and $S_t\ne S_s$, then $S_t$ lies in that closure and has smaller dimension; the incidence relation records exactly these pairs. Each stratum carries its complete model-specified field, operator, boundary, orientation, coorientation, framing, and other label data $\lambda_s$ as required; $J\subseteq S$ is the set of junction strata, and each $S_t$ with $t\in J$ carries a model-specified junction operator $J_t$ with an ordering of all incident labels. The model must declare which such networks and other insertions form admissible inputs of $\mathcal A_{\mathcal T}$ and define their correlators. A one-stratum network with no junction stratum is the preceding single defect, and a list of strata or a picture without its field and junction data is not a defect insertion.

An **isotopy** of a defect network is a smooth one-parameter family of its stratum embeddings $j_{s,t}:\Sigma_s\hookrightarrow M^\circ$, $t\in[0,1]$, compatible on stratum closures and incidence data, whose stratification and incidence relation are unchanged and which creates no additional intersections. The model-specified transport maps carry every stratum label $\lambda_s$, framing or orientation, and junction operator along the family; the combined background and boundary data remain fixed, and the network stays disjoint from every other insertion throughout the deformation. A single-stratum defect is the one-element special case. The insertion is **topological in $\mathcal T$** if, for every complete admissible input containing the selected network, every other insertion data $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ in that input (each of which may itself be an observable or another defect/network), and every such decorated isotopy from $D_0$ to $D_1$ disjoint from all the other insertion data, the model-defined correlators satisfy

$$C_{\mathcal T}(b;D_0;X_1,\ldots,X_n)=C_{\mathcal T}(b;D_1;X_1,\ldots,X_n).$$

This is a property to verify for the specified model and insertion, not an automatic consequence of assigning a defect label or drawing a crossing. No physical quantity with units is introduced here; all dimensional quantities and normalizations remain those declared by $\mathcal T$.

Use the selected-model and defect-insertion data from the preceding defect definition: a model specifies its manifold, background and boundary data, fields with regularity conditions, unit conventions, complete admissible insertion inputs, correlator, and topology on its value space. Let $\mathcal T_-$ and $\mathcal T_+$ be two such models in the same spacetime dimension $d$ on the same smooth manifold $M$. Their metric or signature, background bundles, boundary conditions, field normalizations, and units must either agree or be related by an explicitly supplied identification. No such identification is inferred from names or equal dimensions.

A **codimension-one interface** from $\mathcal T_-$ to $\mathcal T_+$ is data $(\mathcal W,\mathcal I)$ where $\mathcal W\hookrightarrow M^\circ$ is a closed smooth embedded hypersurface with a chosen coorientation and a specified collar $\mathcal W\times(-\epsilon,\epsilon)$, $\epsilon>0$. The negative side uses $\mathcal T_-$ and the positive side uses $\mathcal T_+$. The interface data $\mathcal I$ is a specified local transmission condition, operator map, or boundary condition relating the one-sided field data in that collar, together with any orientation, framing, or junction labels required by the models. The combined model declares its admissible complete inputs, including combined background and boundary data and all other finite insertion data on each side. Write $\Xi_-$ and $\Xi_+$ for those ordered lists; each entry is an ordinary observable insertion or other model-admitted decorated defect/network insertion. The combined model assigns each such input a correlator $C_{\mathcal T_-,\mathcal T_+}(b_-;b_+;\mathcal I(\mathcal W);\Xi_-;\Xi_+)$. The interface is **topological** when, for every such input, this correlator is unchanged under every allowed decorated isotopy of the interface that preserves the source and target side labels and incidence data and crosses no other insertion.

For interfaces $\mathcal I_{01}:\mathcal T_0\to\mathcal T_1$ and $\mathcal I_{12}:\mathcal T_1\to\mathcal T_2$, define their **fusion** only when the model supplies a product collar containing two parallel interfaces at separation $\delta>0$ and a common Hausdorff topological value space $\mathcal V$ for the compared correlators. If the selected models use different value spaces, the model must also specify comparison maps into $\mathcal V$; convergence below means convergence after those maps, in the topology of $\mathcal V$. For every declared complete input with the pair and all other finite insertion data, including ordinary observables and other decorated defects or networks, held fixed outside the shrinking collar, the model must specify $C_\delta\in\mathcal V$ and a correlator $C_0\in\mathcal V$ of a single interface such that $C_\delta\to C_0$ as $\delta\downarrow0$. The model also specifies the limiting insertion's normalization and junction data; when all these requirements hold, it is the fused interface $\mathcal I_{12}\star\mathcal I_{01}:\mathcal T_0\to\mathcal T_2$. If the comparison topology or the required correlator limits are absent, no single fused interface is asserted.

An **endodefect** has $\mathcal T_- = \mathcal T_+$ as the same complete model data, not merely models with similarly named fields. The **transparent identity interface** $\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}$ is the model-supplied transmission condition whose correlator equals the no-interface correlator for every complete admissible input. For an endodefect $\mathcal I$ to induce a symmetry, its data must specify a bijection $\alpha_{\mathcal I}$ on the model's typed local-observable and other-insertion data and a bijection $\beta_{\mathcal I}$ on its combined background and boundary data; these maps must preserve types, supports, algebraic relations, and admissibility. They preserve correlators precisely when, for every admissible input $(b;\mathbf O,D)$,

$$C_{\mathcal T}(\beta_{\mathcal I}(b);\alpha_{\mathcal I}(\mathbf O,D))=C_{\mathcal T}(b;\mathbf O,D).$$

An endodefect is an **invertible symmetry interface** only if a two-sided inverse exists under the stated fusion operation, both composites equal $\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}$ in all declared correlators, and the induced bijections above are automorphisms preserving correlators. A topological interface between distinct source and target models is an interface, not an internal symmetry of either model. No further property is implied by this definition; any additional claim must be formulated and verified for the specified model.

No dimensional quantity is added by this definition. Each model and interface must retain its declared unit system and normalization, and this definition does not assert that a continuum fusion limit exists.

derivations.claim: The matrices satisfy $U_0=I$, $U_1^\dagger=U_1$, and $U_1^2=I$. Hence $g\mapsto U_g$ is a unitary representation of $\mathbb Z_2$. For $X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, direct multiplication gives $U_1 X U_1^{-1}=-X$, so this action is nontrivial.

For every $O\in\operatorname{End}(\mathcal H)$ and density matrix $\rho$, $\operatorname{Tr}(\beta_g(\rho)\alpha_g(O_n)\cdots\alpha_g(O_1))=\operatorname{Tr}(U_g\rho O_n\cdots O_1U_g^{-1})=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho O_n\cdots O_1)$ by cyclicity of the finite-dimensional trace. The same cancellation applies when any factors $O_i$ are admitted defect matrices $U_h$, which are fixed under conjugation. Thus the induced insertion and boundary-data automorphisms preserve every declared complete correlator.

Fix any admissible finite list of other insertion times and move $\tau$ through an allowed decorated isotopy. Since the motion crosses no other insertion or boundary, its relative order with every insertion is fixed. Every propagation factor is $I$ by [A1], so the ordered matrix product, and therefore its trace against every fixed $\rho$, is unchanged. This verifies topologicality for the full declared input set.

For two group defects separated by $\delta>0$, the propagation between them is $e^{-\delta H}=I$ by [A1], so their ordered product is $U_hU_g=U_{h+g}$, independent of $\delta$. With any fixed finite list of other insertions outside their shrinking collar, every declared correlator is unchanged when this adjacent pair is replaced by $U_{h+g}$. Hence the fusion limit exists in the usual topology of $\mathbb C$ for all such correlators, and $U_1U_1=U_0=I$ gives a two-sided inverse.

By [F1] and step 1.3, the point insertion is topological. Step 1.1 gives its nontrivial observable automorphism, step 1.2 verifies correlator covariance including the boundary data, and step 2.1 with [F2] gives group-like fusion and a two-sided inverse. It is therefore an invertible symmetry defect in this finite model only.

derivations.claim: Direct multiplication gives $V^\dagger V=VV^\dagger=I$ and $H_+V=VH_-$. Thus $V$ is unitary and intertwines the source and target Hamiltonians. The assignment $O_-\mapsto VO_-V^\dagger$ is a bijective, product-preserving, adjoint-preserving map of the two full matrix observable algebras, and the corresponding boundary-state map is $\psi\mapsto V\psi$.

From $H_+V=VH_-$, induction gives $H_+^nV=VH_-^n$ for every integer $n\ge0$. Substituting this identity term by term into the convergent finite-matrix exponential series yields $e^{-sH_+}V=Ve^{-sH_-}$ for every $s\ge0$.

For any $s<\tau<t$, step 2.1 gives $E_\tau(t,s)=e^{-(t-\tau)H_+}Ve^{-(\tau-s)H_-}=Ve^{-(t-s)H_-}=e^{-(t-s)H_+}V$, independent of $\tau$. Taking adjoints of $H_+V=VH_-$ also gives $e^{-rH_-}V^\dagger=V^\dagger e^{-rH_+}$ for every $r\ge0$, so the corresponding reverse-interface crossing factor is independent of its position as well. In any fixed finite allowed sequence of forward and reverse interfaces, moving one interface within a gap between fixed insertion times changes only its crossing factor; all other interval factors and insertion maps remain fixed. Therefore every declared finite-list numerator is independent of each interface position, and the same argument with no ordinary insertions makes the normalizer independent. For a single interface, setting $\widehat O_i=VO_iV^\dagger$ when $t_i<\tau$ and $\widehat O_i=O_i$ when $t_i>\tau$ rewrites each source-side factor as a target-model factor, with initial vector $V\psi_-$, terminal vector $\psi_+$, and the same normalizer $Z$. Hence the corresponding target-only normalized matrix element equals $C_\tau$. Thus every normalized correlator is independent of position for all admissible boundary data and insertion lists.

Put the reverse interface $V^\dagger$ a distance $\delta>0$ from $V$, with every other insertion and every other interface fixed outside the shrinking two-interface collar. The transfer factors between the pair are $V^\dagger e^{-\delta H_+}V=e^{-\delta H_-}$ on $\mathcal H_-$ and $Ve^{-\delta H_-}V^\dagger=e^{-\delta H_+}$ on $\mathcal H_+$. These converge to the identity matrices in operator norm as $\delta\downarrow0$. For any fixed finite allowed sequence of other interfaces and ordinary insertions, its numerator is a finite product of fixed matrices and these factors, so it converges to the numerator with the transparent identity interface; its no-ordinary-insertion normalizer converges to the corresponding nonzero identity-interface normalizer by the admissibility condition in the Example. Division is continuous at that nonzero limit, so every declared normalized correlator converges in the usual topology of $\mathbb C$, including those with other interfaces. Thus the fusion limits are both transparent identities. By [F1], step 3.1 verifies topologicality and these limits give the two-sided inverse. Since the two named models have different Hamiltonian matrices, this is an equivalence interface between models, not an internal symmetry of either model before an identification is supplied.

derivations.claim: Regard both models on $[0,T]$, $T>0$, with a point interface at $\tau\in(0,T)$. For the complete source- and target-side lists in [A1], the correlator is $C_\tau=\langle a,B_\ell\cdots B_1J A_k\cdots A_1b\rangle/Z$, because both Hamiltonians vanish. Moving $\tau$ within the gap between the fixed source-side and target-side lists crosses no insertion, leaves their order unchanged, and introduces no nonidentity propagation factor. The numerator and denominator are therefore independent of $\tau$ for every allowed list and boundary pair. This is a topological interface under the full declared input set.

The interface is not an endodefect: its source space is $\mathbb C$ and its target space is $\mathbb C^2$, so the two complete model data are distinct. It also has no two-sided inverse.
